answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 32% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the falcon balance is debited each close, the opal ledger shows the bleed, and the crystal audit lists every fee. An operator holding 249 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
